newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh asks India to review water accord.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh asks India to review water accord.

text.p: Bangladesh has asked neighbour India for immediate talks on water sharing prompted by waning supplies from the mighty Ganges river, Water Resources Minister Abdur Razzak said on Friday.

The opposition Bangladesh Nationalist party (BNP), headed by former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia, has denounced December's water-sharing treaty between Dhaka and New Delhi as a "hoax" and points to the timid Ganges flow as proof.
The government of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has defended the treaty but now appears somewhat perplexed and is trying to find out what has gone wrong.
"We have requested India to immediately sit down to discuss the problem," Razzak told Reuters in an interview.
He said the water flow had begun to subside in March.
"India informed us the flow at the Farakka (barrage) has slowed down. We asked why? India says ice (in the Himalayas where the Ganges originates) is not melting enough to raise the level."
Under the December treaty, if the water flow at the barrage near Bangladesh's northern border falls below 70,000 cusecs (cubic feet per second), the two countries should split the water evenly.
Dr Ainun Nishat, of Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology, said on Wednesday the water flow at Farakka had fallen below 50,000 cusecs.
"Water flow at Hardinge bridge point (in Bangladesh) now fluctuates between 10,000 and 25,000 cusecs. Somwehere there is a problem," he told Reuters.
"We have doubts whether water is being properly released (through the Farakka barrage)," he added.
Razzak said a team from India was expected to arrive in Dhaka shortly to try to sort out the problem.
He said the December treaty had a provision for review if the flow of water at Farakka falls below 50,000 cusecs.
The water treaty at the time appeared to have ended a decades-old dispute between the two countries but it has failed to quieten the foes of Sheikh Hasina.
